lesson.title: 7.7 Would you like to come to my party?
lesson.unit_title: Everyday needs, plans and free time
lesson.unit_outcome: Say what hurts and why someone feels a certain way, describe what people are wearing and the weather as it happens, tell someone to put on or take off clothes, talk about what people like doing, invite and answer, ask someone to repeat or explain, talk about being sick, the months and seasons, compare with the biggest and the tallest, and say what people and animals can do and are good at.
lesson.lesson_title: Would you like to come to my party?
lesson.sub_lesson_title: Would you like to come to my party?
lesson.goal: Invite someone with Would you like to …? and accept with I'd love to! or say no politely with Sorry, I'm busy.
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 7.7 Let's Do Something Together: A1 invites with Do you want to …? and Let's …; A1+ 7.7 invites politely. The one new grammar relationship is Would you like to + a verb (Would you like to come to my party?), which grows A1+ 5.3's Would you like + a thing (Would you like some tea?), answered with I'd love to! or Sorry, I'm busy. Three new photos tell the party story: Sofia invites at her door, Luis says yes with joy, Diego is buried in work; A1 7.7's sofa, park and table invitations come back.
lesson.prerequisite: A1 7.7 Do you want to … and the four activities; A1+ 5.3 Would you like + a thing; A1+ 5.9 I'd like; A1 4.11 come.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Join Would you like to (wud-yuh-LAIK-tuh); say I'd love to! with energy on LOVE. Do not require native-like speed.
